message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Frappe Helpdesk on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- amazon-bedrock: Builds generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore. Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.
- aws-billing-and-cost-management: Analyze AWS costs, find savings, manage budgets, evaluate Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, right-size EC2/Lambda/RDS/EBS with Compute Optimizer, look up service pricing, query CUR with Athena, detect cost anomalies, scope costs to billing views, and monitor Free Tier usage. Triggers on: AWS bill, cost analysis, reduce spend, savings plan, reserved instance, right-size, budget alert, cost optimization, pricing, free tier, cost anomaly, CUR, cost audit, billing view, billing view ARN.
- aws-blocks: Guides building full-stack applications with AWS Blocks — an Infrastructure-from-Code framework. Applies when creating APIs, selecting Building Blocks (KVStore, DistributedTable, Database, AuthBasic, AuthCognito, Realtime, AsyncJob, FileBucket, etc.), running local development, or deploying AWS Blocks applications. Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.
- aws-cdk: Authors, deploys, and troubleshoots AWS infrastructure using CDK with TypeScript or Python. Covers best practices, stack architecture, and construct patterns. Always use when writing CDK constructs, bootstrapping environments, running cdk deploy/synth/diff, fixing CDK or CloudFormation errors, planning stack structure, importing existing resources, resolving drift, or refactoring stacks without resource replacement.
- aws-cloudformation: Author, validate, and troubleshoot AWS CloudFormation templates. Covers template authoring with secure defaults, pre-deployment validation (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, change sets), and root-cause diagnosis of failed stacks using CloudFormation events and CloudTrail correlation.
- aws-containers: Deploys and operates containerized workloads on ECS, Fargate, and ECR. Covers task definitions, Fargate services, ECR repository setup and lifecycle policies, ECS Exec debugging, service scaling, deployment strategies, load balancer integration, and logging configuration. Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.
- aws-messaging-and-streaming: Guides use of AWS messaging and streaming services. Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.
- aws-observability: Builds, configures, debugs, and optimizes AWS observability with CloudWatch (Log Insights, Metrics, Alarms, Dashboards, EMF), X-Ray, CloudTrail, and ADOT (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry), AND enables/onboards services to Application Signals using ADOT auto-instrumentation SDKs. Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Covers cold starts, CORS debugging, event source mappings, troubleshooting, concurrency, SnapStart, Powertools, function URLs, EventBridge Scheduler, Lambda layers, and production readiness. Triggers on mentions of Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, SAM templates, CDK serverless stacks, DynamoDB stream triggers, SQS event sources, cold starts, timeouts, 502/504 errors, throttling, concurrency, CORS, Powertools, or any event-driven architecture on AWS, even without the word "serverless." Does not apply to EC2, ECS/Fargate containers, or Amplify hosting.
- cso: Chief Security Officer mode. (gstack)
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- investigate: Systematic debugging with root cause investigation. (gstack)
- office-hours: YC Office Hours — two modes. (gstack)
- review: Pre-landing PR review. (gstack)
- signing-in-to-aws: Gets AWS credentials for CLI/SDK access via `aws login`. Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/frappe/helpdesk
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0 (plus mariadb:11.8.8 and redis:6.2.23-alpine)
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: "4"
  database: in-compose MariaDB on a named volume. A redu MANAGED database cannot be used here; see the quirks, this is the most important decision in the file
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0486
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: frappe-helpdesk
quirks:
  - "⛔ DO NOT USE THE COMPOSE IN THE helpdesk REPO. docker/docker-compose.yml there is a DEVELOPMENT container and the README files it under \"Development Setup\": the frappe/bench image at its rolling unpinned tag, command \"bash /workspace/init.sh\", the checkout bind-mounted at /workspace, and a MariaDB root password of 123. It builds a bench from source inside the container. The deployable shape is frappe/frappe_docker's pwd.yml with the image swapped for the helpdesk one, which is the compose given further down in this file."
  - "⛔ THE IMAGE IS ON ghcr.io, NOT DOCKER HUB, AND THE ROLLING UNPINNED TAG DOES NOT EXIST. There is no frappe/helpdesk repository on Docker Hub at all: its API answers with an object-not-found message. On ghcr.io the tag list has 53 entries and `latest` is NOT one of them: the manifest API answers 404 for it, so a habit-written `latest` reference fails the pull outright rather than quietly pulling something newer. Use ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0, which existed on 2026-08-17 and was built on 2026-08-05. Do NOT use `stable`: it currently resolves to the same index digest as v1.29.0 but it moves on every release, so a redeploy across a release would silently change your schema. Only linux/amd64 is present in the index, which is what redu runs."
  - "⛔⛔ THE IMAGE TAG DOES NOT NAME THE SOURCE TREE, SO DO NOT TELL THE USER THEY ARE RUNNING THE v1.29.0 SOURCES. Read at that tag: .github/workflows/build.yml exports an APPS_JSON that pins frappe/telephony to the BRANCH \"develop\" and frappe/helpdesk to the BRANCH \"main\", sets FRAPPE_BRANCH=version-15, and tags the result with the release tag and with `stable`. So the image is a build of two moving branches taken on the day that tag was pushed. Pinning the version is still exactly right, because every tag has its own immutable digest; describing what is inside it as a released source tree is not."
  - "⛔⛔ YOU CANNOT USE A redu MANAGED DATABASE FOR THIS, AND THAT DECIDES THE WHOLE SHAPE. bench new-site calls setup_database() (frappe/database/mariadb/setup_db.py:21-52), which opens a connection as the database ROOT user and then runs DROP USER, DROP DATABASE, CREATE USER, CREATE DATABASE, GRANT ALL and FLUSH PRIVILEGES. redu's managed MariaDB provisions exactly one database and one user granted privileges on that database alone, and hands out no root account, so every one of those statements is refused and site creation fails before it starts. Being able to CONNECT to a managed database is not the same as being able to CREATE A SITE in it. Upstream also starts MariaDB with --character-set-server=utf8mb4, --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci and --skip-character-set-client-handshake, which are server-level settings you do not control on a managed instance. So MariaDB runs IN THE COMPOSE, pinned, on a named volume. This matches the frappe-hr entry in this library for the same reason."
  - "⛔ SAY THIS TO THE USER IN THESE WORDS, BEFORE THEY APPROVE THE PLAN: EVERY TICKET AND EVERY ATTACHMENT LIVES ON THE APP VM, NOT IN A MANAGED DATABASE. Almost every other entry in this library keeps its data in a managed database on its own private VM, which survives the app being redeployed. This one cannot, for the reason in the quirk above. The db-data and sites volumes survive container restarts and image updates on that VM; they do NOT survive delete_deployment, and there is no managed database left behind to recover from. Set up backups on day one: `bench --site <site> backup --with-files` writes into the sites volume, and the image ships push_backup.py for sending a backup to S3-compatible storage off the VM. A support desk holding your customers' correspondence with no off-box backup is a bad deploy even when it is a working one."
  - "⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE ACCOUNT IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME, AND IT IS CALLED Administrator. This is the safe shape and it is why this app is in the library at all. The one-shot create-site container runs bench new-site with --admin-password taken from the environment, and until that container has finished the site directory does not exist, so nginx has nothing to serve and there is no window in which a stranger can claim anything. ⛔ THE CATCH IS THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT: helpdesk's own README says, under its Docker instructions, \"Username: Administrator, Password: [REDACTED:value]\", and the dev compose uses it. Generate a long ALPHANUMERIC password instead (alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in a shell or a form body), pass it in through the environment, and prove afterwards with the script in the body of this file that the documented default does NOT work and that yours DOES. You are not fighting upstream here: upstream's own easy-install.py already does this, calling generate_pass() and handing the result to bench new-site --admin-password. Never leave this instance on a public hostname until that check has passed."
  - "⛔ ONE deploy_compose IS ENOUGH, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS ROUTE IS NOT. A Frappe site does not exist until a command creates it, and that command needs the database ROOT password, so there is genuinely a step between \"containers are running\" and \"anything serves\". Upstream's easy-install.py does it as a separate `docker compose exec backend bench new-site` AFTER the stack is up, which would be a second manual step here. The compose in this file does it INSIDE the deploy instead, as a one-shot create-site service ordered behind the configurator, exactly as frappe_docker's pwd.yml does. So a single deploy_compose does produce a working, logged-in-able site. ⚠️ The failure mode to watch for: if create-site fails, the other containers still come up and the hostname serves an nginx error rather than an outage, which reads like a proxy problem. When anything looks wrong, read `sudo docker compose logs create-site` FIRST, before touching anything else."
  - "⛔ THE APP IS AT /helpdesk, NOT AT THE ROOT OF THE HOSTNAME, AND AN ANONYMOUS VISITOR TO / GETS A LOGIN PAGE. helpdesk/hooks.py mounts the SPA with website_route_rules from_route \"/helpdesk/<path:app_path>\". For a Guest with no Website Settings home_page, frappe/website/utils.py:99-127 falls all the way through to \"login\", so https://<host>/ serves the Frappe login form and https://<host>/helpdesk serves the app. Hand the user the /helpdesk URL. If you want the bare hostname to land there, set Website Settings home_page to helpdesk after the first login; do not fake it with a redirect in front of the app."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, CHECKED IN THE SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: exactly four whitelisted methods carry allow_guest. knowledge_base.get_article returns an article but throws a PermissionError for a non-agent whenever its status is not Published; api.config.get_config returns branding fields only (brand name, logo, favicon, a few UI booleans); api.general.get_translations returns the translation bundle; and www/helpdesk/index.get_context_for_dev throws unless developer_mode is on, which it is not here. No ticket, no contact and no customer is reachable without a session. Publishing knowledge-base articles is therefore a deliberate act, which is the correct default for a support desk on a public URL."
  - "SIGNUPS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THE CHAIN IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE YOU SHOULD TEST IT RATHER THAN TRUST IT. frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py:990-992 makes sign_up guest-callable and throws \"Sign Up is disabled\" when is_signup_disabled(); frappe/website/utils.py:197-198 resolves that from Website Settings disable_signup; and version-15's website_settings.json ships that field with a default of 1, described upstream as \"New users will have to be manually registered by system managers.\" So a fresh site refuses anonymous registration, and agents and customers are added by invitation instead. The verify script proves it by CALLING the endpoint, because a default in a JSON file is not the same as the behaviour of the site you just built. ⚠️ If the user later flips that switch (Helpdesk exposes it as Settings, General, Disable signup), note what install.py:setup_customer_role already set up: Portal Settings default_role is \"HD Customer\", so every self-registered stranger lands in the customer portal. That is a deliberate product decision, never a default to drift into."
  - "⛔ THE SITE NAME, FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER AND THE PUBLIC HOSTNAME MUST BE ONE STRING, OR YOU GET A SITE THAT LOADS WITHOUT ITS ASSETS. resources/core/nginx/nginx-template.conf uses server_name ${FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER} and, more importantly, try_files /${FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER}/public/$uri, so the directory under sites/ has to be named exactly that value. Generate the dname yourself in the full `frappe-helpdesk-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form, create the site with that as its name, and set FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER to the same string. A bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Leave the variable unset and nginx-entrypoint.sh defaults it to the literal $host, which then has to be written as a doubled dollar in a compose file to survive interpolation; setting it explicitly avoids that trap entirely."
  - "PORT 8080, AND PUBLISH NOTHING ELSE. The frontend nginx listens on 8080 (nginx-template.conf:16); the gunicorn backend on 8000 and the socketio server on 9000 are internal and must stay unpublished, as must MariaDB's 3306. Pass 8080 to deploy_compose. redu terminates TLS at its own proxy and speaks plain HTTP to that nginx, so set UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For so the app logs the real client IP rather than the proxy's."
  - "⛔ CHANGE THE DATABASE ROOT PASSWORD. frappe_docker's docs/02-setup/04-env-variables.md documents DB_PASSWORD, which is the MariaDB ROOT password, with a default of 123, and helpdesk's dev compose uses that value too. Generate a fresh alphanumeric one and use the SAME value in three places: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD and MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD on the db service, and --db-root-password on the create-site container. Get one of the three wrong and site creation fails with an authentication error that reads like a networking problem."
  - "⛔ USE --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' AND NOT --no-mariadb-socket. frappe/commands/site.py:106-107 prints that --no-mariadb-socket is DEPRECATED and names the replacement. Upstream's own easy-install.py still passes the deprecated flag, so you will see it in tutorials and in their script; frappe_docker's pwd.yml uses the modern one. Copy pwd.yml here, not easy-install.py. The scope matters because the site's database user has to be allowed to connect from the app containers, which are a different host to the db container."
  - "INSTALL ONE APP, NOT TWO. helpdesk/hooks.py:9 declares required_apps = [\"telephony\"], and frappe/installer.py:287-290 installs an app's required_apps BEFORE the app itself, so --install-app helpdesk brings telephony in on its own. Both are already inside the image; --install-app is what installs them INTO the site's database, which is a separate thing from being present in the bench. Do not pass --install-app erpnext: ERPNext is NOT in this image, and asking for it fails the site creation."
  - "THE ORDER OF THE ONE-SHOT CONTAINERS IS LOAD-BEARING, AND SO IS THE COMPOSE ENGINE. configurator writes sites/common_site_config.json with the database and redis hosts and must EXIT SUCCESSFULLY before anything else runs; create-site then waits for db and both redis instances to answer before calling bench new-site. That ordering is expressed with depends_on condition service_completed_successfully, which needs docker compose v2, so force compose_engine docker. ⚠️ Also convert pwd.yml's swarm-style `deploy: restart_policy:` blocks into plain `restart:` keys: ordinary compose IGNORES the deploy section entirely, so a file copied verbatim gives you services that never restart after a reboot."
  - "THE VOLUMES THAT MATTER ARE sites AND db-data, AND sites HOLDS MORE THAN YOU THINK. db-data is MariaDB. sites holds common_site_config.json, the site config, every uploaded and attached file including the private ones, AND the full-text search index, which is a SQLite file rather than a database table: helpdesk/search_sqlite.py sets INDEX_NAME = \"helpdesk_search.db\" and frappe's search/sqlite_search.py:1028-1034 puts it under the site path. All six application containers mount the SAME sites volume, which is not optional: the workers and the scheduler read the site config from it. logs is convenient and disposable, and the redis-queue volume only avoids re-queuing background jobs after a restart."
  - "THE SEARCH INDEX PULLS AN NLTK CORPUS OVER THE INTERNET AFTER EVERY MIGRATE. hooks.py registers helpdesk.search.download_corpus in both after_migrate and the scheduler's `all` events, and it downloads averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng, punkt_tab and brown when they are missing. So the VM needs working outbound HTTPS, which it has, and a first search may be unhelpful until the index has been built in the background. Do not read an empty search result in the first minutes as a broken deploy."
  - "EMAIL IS IMAP POLLING, NOT AN INBOUND MAIL SERVER, WHICH IS WHY THIS APP FITS redu AT ALL. helpdesk/api/settings/email.py creates an Email Account with use_imap 1 and an imap_folder whose append_to is \"HD Ticket\" and folder_name is \"INBOX\". So tickets arrive by the app POLLING a mailbox you already own, and replies go out over your provider's SMTP. Nothing here needs inbound port 25, no PTR record and no mail server. Point it at a real support mailbox in the UI after the first login; a helpdesk with no Email Account is a web form and nothing more."
  - "SIZING, AND UPSTREAM DOES PUBLISH A NUMBER FOR ONCE. frappe_docker docs/02-setup/08-single-server-nginxproxy-example.md:18 recommends 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 50 GB SSD for a single-server production deployment. m1.medium matches its CPU and RAM but has only 40 GB of disk; m1.large meets all three with room at 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB, and disk is the binding constraint here because every emailed attachment lands on this VM. ⚠️ Note this is where this entry deliberately differs from frappe-hr: m1.mem16 costs MORE and has a SMALLER disk (40 GB), so the library's usual \"prefer mem16 over large\" heuristic is the wrong trade for a ticketing system. ⛔ m1.large is ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium, so a trial user cannot deploy this at all: say that BEFORE the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection. RAM use and boot time are unmeasured; measure them on the first run and write the numbers back."
  - "DISK IS WORTH A SENTENCE BEFORE YOU SIZE, BECAUSE GROWING IT LATER IS A VOLUME RESIZE AND NOT A REDEPLOY. The image is 808.3 MB of compressed layers, so roughly 2 to 2.5 GB unpacked, shared by all six application containers. Add MariaDB's data directory, the sites volume where every ticket attachment lands, and the SQLite search index. m1.large comes with 80 GB, which is comfortable for a small support desk and is not comfortable for one whose customers send video."
  - "NO MIGRATION STEP ON THE FIRST DEPLOY, BUT ONE ON EVERY UPDATE. bench new-site builds the schema and runs after_install, which seeds the ticket statuses, the four priorities, a Default SLA, two teams, a welcome ticket and a MariaDB FULLTEXT index. After you change the image tag, however, you MUST run `sudo docker compose exec backend bench --site <site> migrate` before trusting the instance, or it serves a schema older than the code. Frappe does not do this for you and does not warn."
  - "THERE IS AN OPT-IN API LOCKDOWN, OFF BY DEFAULT, AND redu HAS NOT TESTED IT. helpdesk/auth.py registers an auth hook that restricts any account which is not a System User to an explicit allowlist of API paths, and it returns immediately unless the site config key block_endpoints is set. So it does nothing on a stock site. If the user is going to invite external customers into the portal, `bench --site <site> set-config block_endpoints true` is the hardening upstream wrote for exactly that, but turn it on with the user's knowledge and then click through the customer portal yourself, because a whitelist that is missing a route your workflow needs fails as a permission error rather than as anything legible."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.049/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial) AND the data-location warning above, then WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', NO managed database (database is in the compose), port 8080. Generate both passwords yourself and hand them over at the end."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write the compose below locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the helpdesk GitHub URL would land you on the development compose in that repo, which builds a bench from source inside the container and is the single worst outcome available here."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, verified from the LICENSE file, which is the Affero GPL v3 verbatim, and corroborated by helpdesk/hooks.py:11 declaring app_license \"AGPLv3\". ⚠️ awesome-selfhosted's metadata agrees here, but it has been wrong before, so this was read rather than trusted. Running the published image unmodified triggers nothing. Say that plainly to anyone planning to patch it. Note also that this is a stricter licence than frappe-hr's GPL-3.0 in this same library, so do not carry that entry's licence sentence across."
  - "DELETING IT TAKES THE DATA WITH IT, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF MOST ENTRIES HERE. There is no managed database to leave behind and no ongoing database bill after delete_deployment, because the database was never separate. Take a backup off the VM first and confirm the user understands that, then delete."

# Self-host Frappe Helpdesk on redu

An open-source support desk: tickets from email or a customer portal, SLAs, teams, assignment
rules, canned replies and a knowledge base. The official container image on one VM, with a public
HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.049/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Read this before you deploy

**Your tickets live on the app VM, not in a managed database.** Almost every other entry in this
library puts its data in a redu-managed database on its own private VM, so the app can be rebuilt
without touching it. Frappe cannot do that: creating a site requires database ROOT, because `bench
new-site` creates the site's database and its user itself, and a managed database hands out no root
account. So MariaDB runs beside the app, on a named volume.

That is a real, working setup, and it is what every upstream guide describes. It just means
**backups are your job from day one**, and that deleting the deployment deletes your customers'
correspondence with it.

**The app is at `/helpdesk`.** The bare hostname serves the Frappe login page. That is not a
misconfiguration, it is how the app mounts itself; hand people the `/helpdesk` URL.

## What this deploys

- **Frappe Helpdesk** from `ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk`, pinned: an nginx frontend on port 8080, a
  gunicorn backend, a websocket server, two queue workers and the scheduler, all from one image.
- **MariaDB**, pinned, on a named volume, with the character-set flags Frappe's own composes use.
- Two **Redis** instances, one for cache and one for the queue.
- A one-shot **create-site** container that builds the site and sets the Administrator password
  from an environment variable, so the account exists before the URL does.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Frappe Helpdesk on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Ownership, answered plainly

Nobody can claim this instance. The site does not exist until the `create-site` container has
finished, and that container sets the `Administrator` password from a value you generate. Anonymous
signups are refused by Frappe's own default, so agents and customers are added by invitation.

The one thing that can go wrong is using the password from the documentation. Helpdesk's README
tells you to log in as `Administrator` with `admin`. The recipe generates one instead, and the
script below proves the documented one is dead. Upstream's own `easy-install.py` generates one
too, so this is following upstream rather than fighting it.

## The compose to write

Replace nothing by hand except the values in `.env`. `SITE_NAME`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and
`ADMIN_PASSWORD` come from the project `.env`, which you write before uploading.

```yaml
x-app: &app
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [frappe]
  volumes:
    - sites:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites
    - logs:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/logs

services:
  configurator:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        ls -1 apps > sites/apps.txt;
        bench set-config -g db_host $$DB_HOST;
        bench set-config -gp db_port $$DB_PORT;
        bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://$$REDIS_CACHE";
        bench set-config -g redis_queue "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -g redis_socketio "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -gp socketio_port $$SOCKETIO_PORT;
    environment:
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "3306"
      REDIS_CACHE: redis-cache:6379
      REDIS_QUEUE: redis-queue:6379
      SOCKETIO_PORT: "9000"

  create-site:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        wait-for-it -t 180 db:3306;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-cache:6379;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-queue:6379;
        if [ -d "sites/$$SITE_NAME" ]; then
          echo "site $$SITE_NAME already exists, skipping creation";
        else
          bench new-site --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' --db-root-username=root --db-root-password="«REDACTED:assigned:5339dfa8»" --admin-password="«REDACTED:assigned:1a6953cf»" --install-app helpdesk --set-default "$$SITE_NAME";
        fi;
    environment:
      SITE_NAME: "${SITE_NAME}"
      DB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"

  backend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  frontend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on: [backend, websocket]
    command: ["nginx-entrypoint.sh"]
    environment:
      BACKEND: backend:8000
      SOCKETIO: websocket:9000
      FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER: "${SITE_NAME}"
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_RECURSIVE: "off"
      PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT: 120
      CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE: 50m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

  websocket:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "/home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps/frappe/socketio.js"]
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-long:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "long,default,short"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-short:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "short,default"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  scheduler:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "schedule"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  db:
    image: mariadb:11.8.8
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    command:
      - --character-set-server=utf8mb4
      - --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
      - --skip-character-set-client-handshake
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "healthcheck.sh", "--connect", "--innodb_initialized"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/mysql

  redis-cache:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]

  redis-queue:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    volumes:
      - redis-queue-data:/data

networks:
  frappe:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  sites:
  logs:
  db-data:
  redis-queue-data:
```

Write the three values into the project `.env` before you upload. `SITE_NAME` is the full
generated hostname, not a bare label. Generate the passwords alphanumeric, so there is nothing to
escape anywhere downstream:

```bash
printf 'SITE_NAME=%s\n'          "$PUBLIC_HOSTNAME"        >> .env
printf 'DB_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'   "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env
printf 'ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'     "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env
```

## Verify it after boot

Each check is gated on the one before it, and the first is a positive control that proves you are
talking to Helpdesk rather than to an error page. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy while
the containers start, and a Frappe site that was never created answers with its own error page, so
without that gate every "did it NOT do X" assertion below would pass vacuously.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] verify.sh frappe-helpdesk-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?pass the public hostname}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» the Administrator password you passed to bench new-site}"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
API="https://$HOST/api/method"
FORM='content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'

# 1. POSITIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS APP-SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE. A 200 alone would also be satisfied by
#    Frappe's own error page, so require the SPA's own title. This proves the proxy, nginx, the
#    site directory and the helpdesk app being installed into it, all at once.
code="$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/spa.out" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/helpdesk" || echo 000)"
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the stack is still starting. Re-run in a few minutes."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -qi '<title>Helpdesk</title>' "$TMP/spa.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: /helpdesk answered $code without the Helpdesk page title."
  echo "      Read the site-creation log FIRST: sudo docker compose logs create-site"
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: /helpdesk is serving the app (HTTP $code)"

# 2. THE PASSWORD YOU SET MUST WORK. This is also the positive half of check 3: if this fails,
#    a refusal in check 3 would prove nothing about the default.
printf 'usr=Administrator&pwd=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/ok.req"
ok="$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ok.out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/login" \
      -H "$FORM" --data-binary @"$TMP/ok.req" || echo 000)"
if ! grep -q 'Logged In' "$TMP/ok.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: signing in as Administrator returned $ok and not a login."
  echo "      Check that create-site used the password you think it did."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the Administrator password you generated works"

# 3. THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT MUST BE DEAD. Helpdesk's README tells people to log in with it.
printf 'usr=Administrator&pwd=[REDACTED:value]' > "$TMP/bad.req"
bad="$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/bad.out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/login" \
       -H "$FORM" --data-binary @"$TMP/bad.req" || echo 000)"
if grep -q 'Logged In' "$TMP/bad.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: the documented default password STILL WORKS. Anyone who has read the README owns"
  echo "      this instance. Take it off the public hostname now and rebuild the site."
  exit 1
elif grep -q 'Incorrect password' "$TMP/bad.out"; then
  echo "OK: the documented default is refused, and the app said so (HTTP $bad)"
else
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the default login answered $bad without the expected refusal message."
  echo "      Do not assume it failed for the right reason. Read $TMP/bad.out before continuing."
  exit 3
fi

# 4. ANONYMOUS SIGNUP MUST BE REFUSED. Call the endpoint rather than trusting the default; a 404
#    is treated as a failure, because a moved endpoint proves nothing at all.
printf 'email=probe-%s@example.invalid&full_name=probe&redirect_to=/' "$$" > "$TMP/su.req"
su="$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/su.out" -w '%{http_code}' \
      -X POST "$API/frappe.core.doctype.user.user.sign_up" \
      -H "$FORM" --data-binary @"$TMP/su.req" || echo 000)"
if [ "$su" = "404" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the sign_up endpoint is a 404, so this proved nothing. Find the live route"
  echo "      before leaving this instance on a public hostname."
  exit 3
elif grep -q 'Sign Up is disabled' "$T

It builds a bench from source inside the container. The deployable shape is frappe/frappe_docker's pwd.yml with the image swapped for the helpdesk one, which is the compose given further down in this file."

On ghcr.io the tag list has 53 entries and `latest` is NOT one of them: the manifest API answers 404 for it, so a habit-written `latest` reference fails the pull outright rather than quietly pulling something newer. Use ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0, which existed on 2026-08-17 and was built on 2026-08-05. Do NOT use `stable`: it currently resolves to the same index digest as v1.29.0 but it moves on every release, so a redeploy across a release would silently change your schema. Only linux/amd64 is present in the index, which is what redu runs."

So the image is a build of two moving branches taken on the day that tag was pushed. Pinning the version is still exactly right, because every tag has its own immutable digest; describing what is inside it as a released source tree is not."

Being able to CONNECT to a managed database is not the same as being able to CREATE A SITE in it. Upstream also starts MariaDB with --character-set-server=utf8mb4, --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci and --skip-character-set-client-handshake, which are server-level settings you do not control on a managed instance. Generate a long ALPHANUMERIC password instead (alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in a shell or a form body), pass it in through the environment, and prove afterwards with the script in the body of this file that the documented default does NOT work and that yours DOES. # Self-host Frappe Helpdesk on redu

An open-source support desk: tickets from email or a customer portal, SLAs, teams, assignment
rules, canned replies and a knowledge base. The official container image on one VM, with a public
HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.049/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Read this before you deploy

**Your tickets live on the app VM, not in a managed database.** Almost every other entry in this
library puts its data in a redu-managed database on its own private VM, so the app can be rebuilt
without touching it. Frappe cannot do that: creating a site requires database ROOT, because `bench
new-site` creates the site's database and its user itself, and a managed database hands out no root
account. So MariaDB runs beside the app, on a named volume.

That is a real, working setup, and it is what every upstream guide describes. It just means
**backups are your job from day one**, and that deleting the deployment deletes your customers'
correspondence with it.

**The app is at `/helpdesk`.** The bare hostname serves the Frappe login page. That is not a
misconfiguration, it is how the app mounts itself; hand people the `/helpdesk` URL.

## What this deploys

- **Frappe Helpdesk** from `ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk`, pinned: an nginx frontend on port 8080, a
  gunicorn backend, a websocket server, two queue workers and the scheduler, all from one image.
- **MariaDB**, pinned, on a named volume, with the character-set flags Frappe's own composes use.
- Two **Redis** instances, one for cache and one for the queue.
- A one-shot **create-site** container that builds the site and sets the Administrator password
  from an environment variable, so the account exists before the URL does.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Frappe Helpdesk on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Ownership, answered plainly

Nobody can claim this instance. The site does not exist until the `create-site` container has
finished, and that container sets the `Administrator` password from a value you generate. Anonymous
signups are refused by Frappe's own default, so agents and customers are added by invitation.

The one thing that can go wrong is using the password from the documentation. Helpdesk's README
tells you to log in as `Administrator` with `admin`. The recipe generates one instead, and the
script below proves the documented one is dead. Upstream's own `easy-install.py` generates one
too, so this is following upstream rather than fighting it.

## The compose to write

Replace nothing by hand except the values in `.env`. `SITE_NAME`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and
`ADMIN_PASSWORD` come from the project `.env`, which you write before uploading.

```yaml
x-app: &app
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [frappe]
  volumes:
    - sites:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites
    - logs:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/logs

services:
  configurator:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        ls -1 apps > sites/apps.txt;
        bench set-config -g db_host $$DB_HOST;
        bench set-config -gp db_port $$DB_PORT;
        bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://$$REDIS_CACHE";
        bench set-config -g redis_queue "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -g redis_socketio "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -gp socketio_port $$SOCKETIO_PORT;
    environment:
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "3306"
      REDIS_CACHE: redis-cache:6379
      REDIS_QUEUE: redis-queue:6379
      SOCKETIO_PORT: "9000"

  create-site:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        wait-for-it -t 180 db:3306;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-cache:6379;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-queue:6379;
        if [ -d "sites/$$SITE_NAME" ]; then
          echo "site $$SITE_NAME already exists, skipping creation";
        else
          bench new-site --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' --db-root-username=root --db-root-password="«REDACTED:assigned:5339dfa8»" --admin-password="«REDACTED:assigned:1a6953cf»" --install-app helpdesk --set-default "$$SITE_NAME";
        fi;
    environment:
      SITE_NAME: "${SITE_NAME}"
      DB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"

  backend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  frontend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on: [backend, websocket]
    command: ["nginx-entrypoint.sh"]
    environment:
      BACKEND: backend:8000
      SOCKETIO: websocket:9000
      FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER: "${SITE_NAME}"
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_RECURSIVE: "off"
      PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT: 120
      CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE: 50m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

  websocket:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "/home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps/frappe/socketio.js"]
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-long:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "long,default,short"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-short:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "short,default"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  scheduler:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "schedule"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  db:
    image: mariadb:11.8.8
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    command:
      - --character-set-server=utf8mb4
      - --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
      - --skip-character-set-client-handshake
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "healthcheck.sh", "--connect", "--innodb_initialized"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/mysql

  redis-cache:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]

  redis-queue:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    volumes:
      - redis-queue-data:/data

networks:
  frappe:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  sites:
  logs:
  db-data:
  redis-queue-data:
```

Write the three values into the project `.env` before you upload. `SITE_NAME` is the full
generated hostname, not a bare label. Generate the passwords alphanumeric, so there is nothing to
escape anywhere downstream:

```bash
printf 'SITE_NAME=%s\n'          "$PUBLIC_HOSTNAME"        >> .env
printf 'DB_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'   "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env
printf 'ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'     "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env
```

## Verify it after boot

Each check is gated on the one before it, and the first is a positive control that proves you are
talking to Helpdesk rather than to an error page. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy while
the containers start, and a Frappe site that was never created answers with its own error page, so
without that gate every "did it NOT do X" assertion below would pass vacuously.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] verify.sh frappe-helpdesk-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?pass the public hostname}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» the Administrator password you passed to bench new-site}"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
API="https://$HOST/api/method"
FORM='content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'

# 1. POSITIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS APP-SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE. A 200 alone would also be satisfied by
#    Frappe's own error page, so require the SPA's own title. This proves the proxy, nginx, the
#    site directory and the helpdesk app being installed into it, all at once.
code="$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/spa.out" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/helpdesk" || echo 000)"
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the stack is still starting. Re-run in a few minutes."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -qi '<title>Helpdesk</title>' "$TMP/spa.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: /helpdesk answered $code without the Helpdesk page title."
  echo "      Read the site-creation log FIRST: sudo docker compose logs create-site"
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: /helpdesk is serving the app (HTTP $code)"

# 2. THE PASSWORD YOU SET MUST WORK. This is also the positive half of check 3: if this fails,
#    a refusal in check 3 would prove nothing about the default.
printf 'usr=Administrator&pwd=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/ok.req"
ok="$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ok.out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/login" \
      -H "$FORM" --data-binary @"$TMP/ok.req" || echo 000)"
if ! grep -q 'Logged In' "$TMP/ok.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: signing in as Administrator returned $ok and not a login."
  echo "      Check that create-site used the password you think it did."
  exit 1
fi

  - "SIGNUPS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THE CHAIN IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE YOU SHOULD TEST IT RATHER THAN TRUST IT. frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py:990-992 makes sign_up guest-callable and throws \"Sign Up is disabled\" when is_signup_disabled(); frappe/website/utils.py:197-198 resolves that from Website Settings disable_signup; and version-15's website_settings.json ships that field with a default of 1, described upstream as \"New users will have to be manually registered by system managers.\" So a fresh site refuses anonymous registration, and agents and customers are added by invitation instead. A bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Leave the variable unset and nginx-entrypoint.sh defaults it to the literal $host, which then has to be written as a doubled dollar in a compose file to survive interpolation; setting it explicitly avoids that trap entirely."
  - "PORT 8080, AND PUBLISH NOTHING ELSE.   - "⛔ CHANGE THE DATABASE ROOT PASSWORD. frappe_docker's docs/02-setup/04-env-variables.md documents DB_PASSWORD, which is the MariaDB ROOT password, with a default of 123, and helpdesk's dev compose uses that value too. Generate a fresh alphanumeric one and use the SAME value in three places: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD and MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD on the db service, and --db-root-password on the create-site container. Get one of the three wrong and site creation fails with an authentication error that reads like a networking problem."
  - "⛔ USE --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' AND NOT --no-mariadb-socket. frappe/commands/site.py:106-107 prints that --no-mariadb-socket is DEPRECATED and names the replacement. Upstream's own easy-install.py still passes the deprecated flag, so you will see it in tutorials and in their script; frappe_docker's pwd.yml uses the modern one. Copy pwd.yml here, not easy-install.py. The scope matters because the site's database user has to be allowed to connect from the app containers, which are a different host to the db container."
  - "INSTALL ONE APP, NOT TWO. helpdesk/hooks.py:9 declares required_apps = [\"telephony\"], and frappe/installer.py:287-290 installs an app's required_apps BEFORE the app itself, so --install-app helpdesk brings telephony in on its own. Both are already inside the image; --install-app is what installs them INTO the site's database, which is a separate thing from being present in the bench. Do not pass --install-app erpnext: ERPNext is NOT in this image, and asking for it fails the site creation."
  - "THE ORDER OF THE ONE-SHOT CONTAINERS IS LOAD-BEARING, AND SO IS THE COMPOSE ENGINE. configurator writes sites/common_site_config.json with the database and redis hosts and must EXIT SUCCESSFULLY before anything else runs; create-site then waits for db and both redis instances to answer before calling bench new-site.   - "THE VOLUMES THAT MATTER ARE sites AND db-data, AND sites HOLDS MORE THAN YOU THINK. db-data is MariaDB. sites holds common_site_config.json, the site config, every uploaded and attached file including the private ones, AND the full-text search index, which is a SQLite file rather than a database table: helpdesk/search_sqlite.py sets INDEX_NAME = \"helpdesk_search.db\" and frappe's search/sqlite_search.py:1028-1034 puts it under the site path. All six application containers mount the SAME sites volume, which is not optional: the workers and the scheduler read the site config from it. logs is convenient and disposable, and the redis-queue volume only avoids re-queuing background jobs after a restart."
  - "THE SEARCH INDEX PULLS AN NLTK CORPUS OVER THE INTERNET AFTER EVERY MIGRATE. hooks.py registers helpdesk.search.download_corpus in both after_migrate and the scheduler's `all` events, and it downloads averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng, punkt_tab and brown when they are missing. So the VM needs working outbound HTTPS, which it has, and a first search may be unhelpful until the index has been built in the background. Do not read an empty search result in the first minutes as a broken deploy."
  - "EMAIL IS IMAP POLLING, NOT AN INBOUND MAIL SERVER, WHICH IS WHY THIS APP FITS redu AT ALL. helpdesk/api/settings/email.py creates an Email Account with use_imap 1 and an imap_folder whose append_to is \"HD Ticket\" and folder_name is \"INBOX\". So tickets arrive by the app POLLING a mailbox you already own, and replies go out over your provider's SMTP. Nothing here needs inbound port 25, no PTR record and no mail server. Point it at a real support mailbox in the UI after the first login; a helpdesk with no Email Account is a web form and nothing more."
  - "SIZING, AND UPSTREAM DOES PUBLISH A NUMBER FOR ONCE. frappe_docker docs/02-setup/08-single-server-nginxproxy-example.md:18 recommends 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 50 GB SSD for a single-server production deployment. m1.medium matches its CPU and RAM but has only 40 GB of disk; m1.large meets all three with room at 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB, and disk is the binding constraint here because every emailed attachment lands on this VM. ⚠️ Note this is where this entry deliberately differs from frappe-hr: m1.mem16 costs MORE and has a SMALLER disk (40 GB), so the library's usual \"prefer mem16 over large\" heuristic is the wrong trade for a ticketing system. ⛔ m1.large is ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium, so a trial user cannot deploy this at all: say that BEFORE the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection. RAM use and boot time are unmeasured; measure them on the first run and write the numbers back."
  - "DISK IS WORTH A SENTENCE BEFORE YOU SIZE, BECAUSE GROWING IT LATER IS A VOLUME RESIZE AND NOT A REDEPLOY. The image is 808.3 MB of compressed layers, so roughly 2 to 2.5 GB unpacked, shared by all six application containers. Add MariaDB's data directory, the sites volume where every ticket attachment lands, and the SQLite search index. m1.large comes with 80 GB, which is comfortable for a small support desk and is not comfortable for one whose customers send video."
  - "NO MIGRATION STEP ON THE FIRST DEPLOY, BUT ONE ON EVERY UPDATE. bench new-site builds the schema and runs after_install, which seeds the ticket statuses, the four priorities, a Default SLA, two teams, a welcome ticket and a MariaDB FULLTEXT index. After you change the image tag, however, you MUST run `sudo docker compose exec backend bench --site <site> migrate` before trusting the instance, or it serves a schema older than the code. Frappe does not do this for you and does not warn."
  - "THERE IS AN OPT-IN API LOCKDOWN, OFF BY DEFAULT, AND redu HAS NOT TESTED IT. helpdesk/auth.py registers an auth hook that restricts any account which is not a System User to an explicit allowlist of API paths, and it returns immediately unless the site config key block_endpoints is set. So it does nothing on a stock site. If the user is going to invite external customers into the portal, `bench --site <site> set-config block_endpoints true` is the hardening upstream wrote for exactly that, but turn it on with the user's knowledge and then click through the customer portal yourself, because a whitelist that is missing a route your workflow needs fails as a permission error rather than as anything legible."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.049/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial) AND the data-location warning above, then WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', NO managed database (database is in the compose), port 8080. Generate both passwords yourself and hand them over at the end."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write the compose below locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the helpdesk GitHub URL would land you on the development compose in that repo, which builds a bench from source inside the container and is the single worst outcome available here."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, verified from the LICENSE file, which is the Affero GPL v3 verbatim, and corroborated by helpdesk/hooks.py:11 declaring app_license \"AGPLv3\". ⚠️ awesome-selfhosted's metadata agrees here, but it has been wrong before, so this was read rather than trusted. The user-is-operator test passes: you deploy it into your own account and run it yourself. ⚠️ AGPL SECTION 13 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS TO AN OPERATOR RATHER THAN A DISTRIBUTOR: if you MODIFY helpdesk and let other people use it over the network, including your own customers in the portal, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified triggers nothing. Say that plainly to anyone planning to patch it. Note also that this is a stricter licence than frappe-hr's GPL-3.0 in this same library, so do not carry that entry's licence sentence across."
  - "DELETING IT TAKES THE DATA WITH IT, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF MOST ENTRIES HERE. There is no managed database to leave behind and no ongoing database bill after delete_deployment, because the database was never separate. Take a backup off the VM first and confirm the user understands that, then delete."
---

# Self-host Frappe Helpdesk on redu

An open-source support desk: tickets from email or a customer portal, SLAs, teams, assignment
rules, canned replies and a knowledge base. The official container image on one VM, with a public
HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.049/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Read this before you deploy

**Your tickets live on the app VM, not in a managed database.** Almost every other entry in this
library puts its data in a redu-managed database on its own private VM, so the app can be rebuilt
without touching it. Frappe cannot do that: creating a site requires database ROOT, because `bench
new-site` creates the site's database and its user itself, and a managed database hands out no root

# Self-host Frappe Helpdesk on redu

An open-source support desk: tickets from email or a customer portal, SLAs, teams, assignment
rules, canned replies and a knowledge base. The official container image on one VM, with a public
HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.049/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Read this before you deploy

**Your tickets live on the app VM, not in a managed database.** Almost every other entry in this
library puts its data in a redu-managed database on its own private VM, so the app can be rebuilt
without touching it. Frappe cannot do that: creating a site requires database ROOT, because `bench
new-site` creates the site's database and its user itself, and a managed database hands out no root

new-site` creates the site's database and its user itself, and a managed database hands out no root
account. So MariaDB runs beside the app, on a named volume.

That is a real, working setup, and it is what every upstream guide describes. It just means
**backups are your job from day one**, and that deleting the deployment deletes your customers'
correspondence with it.

**The app is at `/helpdesk`.** The bare hostname serves the Frappe login page. That is not a
misconfiguration, it is how the app mounts itself; hand people the `/helpdesk` URL.

## What this deploys

- **Frappe Helpdesk** from `ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk`, pinned: an nginx frontend on port 8080, a
  gunicorn backend, a websocket server, two queue workers and the scheduler, all from one image.
- **MariaDB**, pinned, on a named volume, with the character-set flags Frappe's own composes use.
- Two **Redis** instances, one for cache and one for the queue.
- A one-shot **create-site** container that builds the site and sets the Administrator password
  from an environment variable, so the account exists before the URL does.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Frappe Helpdesk on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Ownership, answered plainly

Nobody can claim this instance. The site does not exist until the `create-site` container has
finished, and that container sets the `Administrator` password from a value you generate. Anonymous
signups are refused by Frappe's own default, so agents and customers are added by invitation.

The one thing that can go wrong is using the password from the documentation. Helpdesk's README
tells you to log in as `Administrator` with `admin`. The recipe generates one instead, and the
script below proves the documented one is dead. Upstream's own `easy-install.py` generates one
too, so this is following upstream rather than fighting it.

## The compose to write

Replace nothing by hand except the values in `.env`. `SITE_NAME`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and
`ADMIN_PASSWORD` come from the project `.env`, which you write before uploading.

```yaml
x-app: &app
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [frappe]
  volumes:
    - sites:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites
    - logs:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/logs

services:
  configurator:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        ls -1 apps > sites/apps.txt;
        bench set-config -g db_host $$DB_HOST;
        bench set-config -gp db_port $$DB_PORT;
        bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://$$REDIS_CACHE";
        bench set-config -g redis_queue "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -g redis_socketio "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -gp socketio_port $$SOCKETIO_PORT;
    environment:
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "3306"
      REDIS_CACHE: redis-cache:6379
      REDIS_QUEUE: redis-queue:6379
      SOCKETIO_PORT: "9000"

  create-site:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        wait-for-it -t 180 db:3306;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-cache:6379;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-queue:6379;
        if [ -d "sites/$$SITE_NAME" ]; then
          echo "site $$SITE_NAME already exists, skipping creation";
        else
          bench new-site --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' --db-root-username=root --db-root-password="«REDACTED:assigned:5339dfa8»" --admin-password="«REDACTED:assigned:1a6953cf»" --install-app helpdesk --set-default "$$SITE_NAME";
        fi;
    environment:
      SITE_NAME: "${SITE_NAME}"
      DB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"

  backend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  frontend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on: [backend, websocket]
    command: ["nginx-entrypoint.sh"]
    environment:
      BACKEND: backend:8000
      SOCKETIO: websocket:9000
      FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER: "${SITE_NAME}"
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_RECURSIVE: "off"
      PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT: 120
      CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE: 50m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

  websocket:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "/home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps/frappe/socketio.js"]
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-long:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "long,default,short"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-short:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "short,default"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

Write the three values into the project `.env` before you upload. `SITE_NAME` is the full
generated hostname, not a bare label. Generate the passwords alphanumeric, so there is nothing to
escape anywhere downstream:

```bash
printf 'SITE_NAME=%s\n'          "$PUBLIC_HOSTNAME"        >> .env
printf 'DB_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'   "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env
printf 'ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]\n'     "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" >> .env

## Verify it after boot

Each check is gated on the one before it, and the first is a positive control that proves you are
talking to Helpdesk rather than to an error page. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy while
the containers start, and a Frappe site that was never created answers with its own error page, so
without that gate every "did it NOT do X" assertion below would pass vacuously.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] verify.sh frappe-helpdesk-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?pass the public hostname}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» the Administrator password you passed to bench new-site}"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
API="https://$HOST/api/method"
FORM='content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'

# 1. POSITIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS APP-SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE. A 200 alone would also be satisfied by
#    Frappe's own error page, so require the SPA's own title. This proves the proxy, nginx, the
#    site directory and the helpdesk app being installed into it, all at once.
code="$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/spa.out" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/helpdesk" || echo 000)"
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the stack is still starting. Re-run in a few minutes."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -qi '<title>Helpdesk</title>' "$TMP/spa.out"; then
  echo "FAIL: /helpdesk answered $code without the Helpdesk page title."
  echo "      Read the site-creation log FIRST: sudo docker compose logs create-site"
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: /helpdesk is serving the app (HTTP $code)"

# 2. THE PASSWORD YOU SET MUST WORK. This is also the positive half of check 3: if this fails,
#    a refusal in check 3 would prove nothing about the default.
printf 'usr=Administrator&pwd=[REDACTED:value]' "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/ok.req"
ok="$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ok.out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/login" \
