platform_facts: THE deploy VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. The compose project is named app-src, so containers are app-src-<service>-1 and volumes are app-src_<name>. Use `sudo docker ...` on the VM; podman is not installed. Several deploys rediscovered this independently.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM. Call get_env_keys for the NAMES first (no SSH, values never leave the VM); only if you need an actual VALUE, SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read that one key, `sudo grep '^PGPASSWORD=' /opt/app-src/.env`. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback. ⭐ MEASURED over 38 deploys: of 241 ssh escapes, 146 (61%) were exactly these four things, and the four tools were called 11 times. They are faster than a login, they cost the VM nothing extra (the reading is already cached), and reaching for ssh to run `docker ps` is the single most common wasted minute in a deploy.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

x-app: &app
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [frappe]
  volumes:
    - sites:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites
    - logs:/home/frappe/frappe-bench/logs

services:
  configurator:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        ls -1 apps > sites/apps.txt;
        bench set-config -g db_host $$DB_HOST;
        bench set-config -gp db_port $$DB_PORT;
        bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://$$REDIS_CACHE";
        bench set-config -g redis_queue "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -g redis_socketio "redis://$$REDIS_QUEUE";
        bench set-config -gp socketio_port $$SOCKETIO_PORT;
    environment:
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "3306"
      REDIS_CACHE: redis-cache:6379
      REDIS_QUEUE: redis-queue:6379
      SOCKETIO_PORT: "9000"

  create-site:
    <<: *app
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - >
        wait-for-it -t 180 db:3306;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-cache:6379;
        wait-for-it -t 180 redis-queue:6379;
        if [ -d "sites/$$SITE_NAME" ]; then
          echo "site $$SITE_NAME already exists, skipping creation";
        else
          bench new-site --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' --db-root-username=root --db-root-password="«REDACTED:assigned:5339dfa8»" --admin-password="«REDACTED:assigned:1a6953cf»" --install-app helpdesk --set-default "$$SITE_NAME";
        fi;
    environment:
      SITE_NAME: "${SITE_NAME}"
      DB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"

  backend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  frontend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on: [backend, websocket]
    command: ["nginx-entrypoint.sh"]
    environment:
      BACKEND: backend:8000
      SOCKETIO: websocket:9000
      FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER: "${SITE_NAME}"
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For
      UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_RECURSIVE: "off"
      PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT: 120
      CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE: 50m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

  websocket:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "/home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps/frappe/socketio.js"]
    depends_on:
      configurator:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-long:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "long,default,short"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  queue-short:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "worker", "--queue", "short,default"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  scheduler:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bench", "schedule"]
    depends_on:
      create-site:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  db:
    image: mariadb:11.8.8
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    command:
      - --character-set-server=utf8mb4
      - --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
      - --skip-character-set-client-handshake
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "healthcheck.sh", "--connect", "--innodb_initialized"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/mysql

  redis-cache:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]

  redis-queue:
    image: redis:6.2.23-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frappe]
    volumes:
      - redis-queue-data:/data

networks:
  frappe:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  sites:
  logs:
  db-data:
  redis-queue-data:

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/frappe/helpdesk
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0 (plus mariadb:11.8.8 and redis:6.2.23-alpine)
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: "4"
  database: in-compose MariaDB on a named volume. A redu MANAGED database cannot be used here; see the quirks, this is the most important decision in the file
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0486
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: frappe-helpdesk
quirks:
  - "DO NOT USE THE COMPOSE IN THE helpdesk REPO. docker/docker-compose.yml there is a DEVELOPMENT container filed under Development Setup: the frappe/bench image at its rolling unpinned tag, command bash /workspace/init.sh, the checkout bind-mounted at /workspace, and a MariaDB root password of 123. It builds a bench from source inside the container. The deployable shape is frappe_docker's pwd.yml with the image swapped for the helpdesk one, which is the compose given further down in this file."
  - "THE IMAGE IS ON ghcr.io, NOT DOCKER HUB, AND THE ROLLING UNPINNED TAG DOES NOT EXIST. Use ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0. Do NOT use stable: it moves on every release. Only linux/amd64 is present in the index, which is what redu runs."
  - "THE IMAGE TAG DOES NOT NAME THE SOURCE TREE. The build pins frappe/telephony to branch develop and frappe/helpdesk to branch main with FRAPPE_BRANCH=version-15, so the image is a build of two moving branches taken on the day that tag was pushed. Pinning the version is still right; describing it as a released source tree is not."
  - "YOU CANNOT USE A redu MANAGED DATABASE FOR THIS, AND THAT DECIDES THE WHOLE SHAPE. bench new-site calls setup_database(), which connects as database ROOT and runs DROP USER, DROP DATABASE, CREATE USER, CREATE DATABASE, GRANT ALL and FLUSH PRIVILEGES. redu's managed MariaDB provisions one database and one scoped user and hands out no root account, so site creation fails before it starts. Upstream also needs server-level --character-set-server=utf8mb4, --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci and --skip-character-set-client-handshake. So MariaDB runs IN THE COMPOSE, pinned, on a named volume."
  - "SAY THIS TO THE USER BEFORE THEY APPROVE: EVERY TICKET AND EVERY ATTACHMENT LIVES ON THE APP VM, NOT IN A MANAGED DATABASE. The db-data and sites volumes survive container restarts and image updates; they do NOT survive delete_deployment, and there is no managed database left behind to recover from. Set up backups on day one: bench --site <site> backup --with-files writes into the sites volume, and the image ships push_backup.py for S3-compatible storage off the VM."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE ACCOUNT IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME AND IT IS CALLED Administrator. The one-shot create-site container runs bench new-site with --admin-password from the environment, and until it finishes the site directory does not exist, so there is no window in which a stranger can claim anything. THE CATCH IS THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT: helpdesk's README says Username: Administrator, Password: «REDACTED:assigned:d7efb02b» Generate a long ALPHANUMERIC password instead, pass it through the environment, and prove afterwards that the documented default does NOT work and yours DOES."
  - "ONE deploy_compose IS ENOUGH. A Frappe site does not exist until a command creates it, and that command needs the database ROOT password. The compose does it INSIDE the deploy as a one-shot create-site service ordered behind the configurator, exactly as frappe_docker's pwd.yml does. Failure mode: if create-site fails, the other containers still come up and the hostname serves an nginx error rather than an outage. When anything looks wrong, read sudo docker compose logs create-site FIRST."
  - "THE APP IS AT /helpdesk, NOT AT THE ROOT OF THE HOSTNAME. hooks.py mounts the SPA with website_route_rules from_route /helpdesk/<path:app_path>. For a Guest with no home_page, Frappe falls through to login, so https://<host>/ serves the Frappe login form and https://<host>/helpdesk serves the app. Hand the user the /helpdesk URL."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: exactly four whitelisted methods carry allow_guest - knowledge_base.get_article (PermissionError unless Published), api.config.get_config (branding only), api.general.get_translations, and www/helpdesk/index.get_context_for_dev (throws unless developer_mode). No ticket, contact or customer is reachable without a session."
  - "SIGNUPS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT. user.py makes sign_up guest-callable and throws Sign Up is disabled when is_signup_disabled(); website_settings.json ships disable_signup default 1. Test it by CALLING the endpoint rather than trusting the default. If the user later flips it, Portal Settings default_role is HD Customer, so self-registered strangers land in the customer portal."
  - "THE SITE NAME, FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER AND THE PUBLIC HOSTNAME MUST BE ONE STRING, OR YOU GET A SITE THAT LOADS WITHOUT ITS ASSETS. nginx-template.conf uses server_name ${FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER} and try_files /${FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER}/public/$uri, so the directory under sites/ has to be named exactly that value. Generate the dname yourself in the full frappe-helpdesk-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form, create the site with that name, and set FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER to the same string. A bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "PORT 8080, AND PUBLISH NOTHING ELSE. The frontend nginx listens on 8080; the gunicorn backend on 8000 and socketio on 9000 are internal and must stay unpublished, as must MariaDB's 3306. redu terminates TLS at its own proxy and speaks plain HTTP to nginx, so set UPSTREAM_REAL_IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For."
  - "CHANGE THE DATABASE ROOT PASSWORD. DB_PASSWORD is the MariaDB ROOT password and upstream documents a default of 123. Generate a fresh alphanumeric one and use the SAME value in three places: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD and MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD on the db service, and --db-root-password on create-site. Get one of the three wrong and site creation fails with an authentication error that reads like a networking problem."
  - "USE --mariadb-user-host-login-scope='%' AND NOT --no-mariadb-socket, which frappe prints as DEPRECATED. Upstream's easy-install.py still passes the deprecated flag; frappe_docker's pwd.yml uses the modern one. Copy pwd.yml here."
  - "INSTALL ONE APP, NOT TWO. hooks.py declares required_apps = [telephony] and frappe's installer installs required_apps BEFORE the app itself, so --install-app helpdesk brings telephony in on its own. Do not pass --install-app erpnext: ERPNext is NOT in this image and asking for it fails site creation."
  - "THE ORDER OF THE ONE-SHOT CONTAINERS IS LOAD-BEARING, AND SO IS THE COMPOSE ENGINE. configurator writes sites/common_site_config.json and must EXIT SUCCESSFULLY before anything else runs; create-site then waits for db and both redis instances. Also convert pwd.yml's swarm-style deploy: restart_policy: blocks into plain restart: keys - ordinary compose IGNORES the deploy section entirely."
  - "THE VOLUMES THAT MATTER ARE sites AND db-data. db-data is MariaDB. sites holds common_site_config.json, the site config, every uploaded and attached file including private ones, AND the full-text search index, which is a SQLite file (helpdesk_search.db) under the site path. All six application containers mount the SAME sites volume, which is not optional. logs is disposable, and redis-queue-data only avoids re-queuing background jobs after a restart."
  - "THE SEARCH INDEX PULLS AN NLTK CORPUS OVER THE INTERNET AFTER EVERY MIGRATE (averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng, punkt_tab, brown). The VM needs working outbound HTTPS, which it has, and a first search may be unhelpful until the index has been built in the background."
  - "EMAIL IS IMAP POLLING, NOT AN INBOUND MAIL SERVER, WHICH IS WHY THIS APP FITS redu AT ALL. Tickets arrive by the app POLLING a mailbox you already own, and replies go out over your provider's SMTP. Nothing needs inbound port 25, no PTR record and no mail server. Point it at a real support mailbox in the UI after the first login."
  - "SIZING: frappe_docker's single-server doc recommends 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 50 GB SSD. m1.medium matches CPU and RAM but has only 40 GB of disk; m1.large meets all three at 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB, and disk is the binding constraint because every emailed attachment lands on this VM. Note this deliberately differs from frappe-hr: m1.mem16 costs MORE and has a SMALLER disk. m1.large is ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium, so a trial user cannot deploy this at all: say that BEFORE the plan is approved. RAM use and boot time are unmeasured."
  - "DISK IS WORTH A SENTENCE BEFORE YOU SIZE. The image is 808.3 MB compressed, roughly 2 to 2.5 GB unpacked, shared by all six application containers. Add MariaDB's data directory, the sites volume where every attachment lands, and the SQLite search index. m1.large's 80 GB is comfortable for a small support desk and not for one whose customers send video."
  - "NO MIGRATION STEP ON THE FIRST DEPLOY, BUT ONE ON EVERY UPDATE. bench new-site builds the schema and runs after_install, seeding ticket statuses, four priorities, a Default SLA, two teams, a welcome ticket and a MariaDB FULLTEXT index. After you change the image tag you MUST run sudo docker compose exec backend bench --site <site> migrate before trusting the instance."
  - "THERE IS AN OPT-IN API LOCKDOWN, OFF BY DEFAULT, AND redu HAS NOT TESTED IT. helpdesk/auth.py restricts non-System-Users to an allowlist of API paths, but returns immediately unless the site config key block_endpoints is set. bench --site <site> set-config block_endpoints true is the hardening upstream wrote for inviting external customers into the portal; turn it on with the user's knowledge and click through the portal yourself."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.049/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial) AND the data-location warning above, then WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id m1.large, NO managed database (database is in the compose), port 8080. Generate both passwords yourself and hand them over at the end."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write the compose below locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the helpdesk GitHub URL would land you on the development compose in that repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, verified from the LICENSE file and corroborated by hooks.py declaring app_license AGPLv3. The user-is-operator test passes. AGPL SECTION 13 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS TO AN OPERATOR: if you MODIFY helpdesk and let other people use it over the network, including your own customers in the portal, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified triggers nothing. This is a stricter licence than frappe-hr's GPL-3.0."
  - "DELETING IT TAKES THE DATA WITH IT. There is no managed database to leave behind and no ongoing database bill after delete_deployment, because the database was never separate. Take a backup off the VM first and confirm the user understands that, then delete."

# Self-host Frappe Helpdesk on redu

An open-source support desk: tickets from email or a customer portal, SLAs, teams, assignment
rules, canned replies and a knowledge base. The official container image on one VM, with a public
HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.049/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. Above the no-card trial ceiling, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Read this before you deploy

Your tickets live on the app VM, not in a managed database. Frappe cannot use a managed database:
creating a site requires database ROOT, because bench new-site creates the site's database and its
user itself, and a managed database hands out no root account. So MariaDB runs beside the app, on a
named volume. That means backups are your job from day one, and deleting the deployment deletes
your customers' correspondence with it.

The app is at /helpdesk. The bare hostname serves the Frappe login page.

## What this deploys

- Frappe Helpdesk from ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk, pinned: an nginx frontend on port 8080, a
  gunicorn backend, a websocket server, two queue workers and the scheduler, all from one image.
- MariaDB, pinned, on a named volume, with the character-set flags Frappe's own composes use.
- Two Redis instances, one for cache and one for the queue.
- A one-shot create-site container that builds the site and sets the Administrator password
  from an environment variable, so the account exists before the URL does.
- A public hostname on *.redu.cloud with TLS.

## Verify it after boot

A gated script: (1) GET /helpdesk must be 200 AND contain <title>Helpdesk</title>, treating 502 as
INCONCLUSIVE while the stack starts; (2) POST /api/method/login as Administrator with the generated
password must return Logged In; (3) the same call with the documented default admin must be refused
with Incorrect password; (4) POST /api/method/frappe.core.doctype.user.user.sign_up must answer
Sign Up is disabled, treating 404 as INCONCLUSIVE.

## The three that actually break it

The managed database that is not there. The site name (nginx resolves both server name and every
static-file path from FRAPPE_SITE_NAME_HEADER). The documented password.

content.text:
I've written `redu-deploy-plan.md` to the project. **Nothing has been provisioned yet** — here's the plan and cost, and I need your explicit go before I create anything billed.

## Frappe Helpdesk on redu — the plan

**One VM, `m1.large`** (4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB) running an 11-service compose stack from `ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0` (pinned), plus `mariadb:11.8.8` and two `redis:6.2.23-alpine`. Public HTTPS at a pre-generated hostname, port 8080.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Cost** | **GBP 0.0486/hr — about GBP 35.48/month**, billed hourly, delete anytime |
| **Quota** | fits (1/10 instances, 4/20 vCPU, 8/50 GB RAM) |
| **URL** | `https://frappe-helpdesk-38ywi8ku.redu.cloud/helpdesk` |
| **Login** | `Administrator` + a 40-char password I generated (not the README's `admin`) |

### Three things to read before you say go

**1. This is above the no-card trial ceiling.** `m1.large` exceeds `m1.medium`, so this needs a payment method on the account. Your quota check passed, but that's a quota check, not a billing check.

**2. Every ticket and every attachment lives on the app VM, not in a managed database.** This is the one entry in the library that can't use managed Postgres/MariaDB, and it's not a shortcut I took — `bench new-site` connects as database *root* and runs `DROP USER`, `CREATE DATABASE`, `GRANT ALL` itself, and a managed instance hands out no root account. It also needs server-level charset flags you don't control on managed. So MariaDB runs in the compose on a named volume.

The consequence: the `db-data` and `sites` volumes survive container restarts and image updates, but they do **not** survive `delete_deployment`, and there's no managed database left behind to recover from. **Backups are your job from day one** — `bench --site <site> backup --with-files` writes into the sites volume, and the image ships `push_backup.py` for shipping one to S3-compatible storage off the VM. A support desk holding your customers' correspondence with no off-box backup is a bad deploy even when it's a working one.

**3. The app is at `/helpdesk`, not at the root.** The bare hostname serves the Frappe login form — that's how the SPA mounts itself, not a misconfiguration.

### What I've already done (unbilled)

- Extracted the compose verbatim from `redu.md` → `docker-compose.yml` (validated as YAML: 11 services, 4 volumes, `8080:8080`). The repo's own `docker/docker-compose.yml` is a *development* container and is not being used.
- Generated `.env` (chmod 600) with the site name and two 40-char hex passwords — DB root and Administrator. These get passed to the deploy call rather than uploaded, since `prepare_upload` strips `.env`.
- Extracted the gated `verify.sh` to run after boot: it proves `/helpdesk` serves the real SPA, that my password works, that the README's `admin` default is **dead**, and that anonymous signup is refused.

Expect a **10–20 minute settle** — the one-shot `configurator` → `create-site` chain has to finish before anything serves, and a 502 during that window is normal, not a failure.

**Say go and I'll deploy.**
Approved — deploying now.

content.text:
Now I understand the failure completely. Upstream's workflow *does* build with `APPS_JSON` containing telephony + helpdesk via frappe_docker's layered Containerfile — but **the image it publishes doesn't contain them**. The recipe in `redu.md` was written from reading that workflow, not from inspecting the resulting image.

That's a real defect in the recipe's central premise, and it can't be worked around with compose flags — the app simply isn't in the artifact. The only route to a working Helpdesk is to build the image the way upstream's own workflow intends. I'm proceeding with that rather than stopping, since it's the same VM, same flavor, same cost, and it's the only path to what you asked for.

Both resolved definitively, and check 3 passes for the right reason — the script's expected string is just outdated:

- **Default password refused:** HTTP 401, `AuthenticationError` — *"Invalid login credentials"*. Frappe 15.116.1 changed the wording from `Incorrect password`, which is why the script couldn't confirm it.
- **Anonymous signup refused:** HTTP 417, `ValidationError: Sign Up is disabled`.

The app is verified working, but I need to flag a discrepancy rather than let it pass: [REDACTED:value]'s deployment record is `status: error`, `terminal: true`.** That was recorded at 21:24 from the *original* failure — its build log is the old `No module named 'helpdesk'` trace. redu's probe window closed before I repaired the stack, so the platform row stays failed even though `containers_summary` shows everything running and the public URL serves the app.

Let me capture what I learned into the repo files. First the working build, so it's reproducible:

input.command:
cat > build-image.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build a Frappe Helpdesk image that ACTUALLY CONTAINS the helpdesk app.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the published ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk images do NOT contain
# Frappe Helpdesk. They are a bare frappe bench. Verified 2026-08-20 on tags
# v1.29.0, stable, main and v1.28.1: /home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps holds only
# "frappe", and `import helpdesk` raises ModuleNotFoundError.
#
# ROOT CAUSE: helpdesk's .github/workflows/build.yml passes the apps list as
#   --build-arg APPS_JSON_BASE64=...
# but frappe_docker's images/layered/Containerfile now reads it from a BuildKit
# SECRET MOUNT (--mount=type=secret,id=apps_json,target=/opt/frappe/apps.json).
# An unconsumed build-arg is not an error, so the build silently produces a
# frappe-only bench and pushes it under the helpdesk name.
#
# Run this ON THE DEPLOY VM before `docker compose up`.
set -euo pipefail

IMAGE_TAG="${IMAGE_TAG:-helpdesk-local:v1.29.0}"
HELPDESK_REF="${HELPDESK_REF:-v1.29.0}"   # pinned tag, not the moving "main"
TELEPHONY_REF="${TELEPHONY_REF:-develop}" # upstream has no tags for telephony
FRAPPE_BRANCH="${FRAPPE_BRANCH:-version-15}"
BUILD_DIR="${BUILD_DIR:-/opt/fd-build}"

sudo rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"
sudo git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/frappe/frappe_docker "$BUILD_DIR"
cd "$BUILD_DIR"

printf '%s' "[{\"url\":\"https://github.com/frappe/telephony\",\"branch\":\"$TELEPHONY_REF\"},{\"url\":\"https://github.com/frappe/helpdesk\",\"branch\":\"$HELPDESK_REF\"}]" \
  | sudo tee "$BUILD_DIR/apps.json" >/dev/null

# CACHE_BUST is load-bearing: a secret mount does NOT invalidate the BuildKit
# cache, so without it a rebuild silently reuses a previous frappe-only layer.
sudo DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
  -f images/layered/Containerfile \
  -t "$IMAGE_TAG" \
  --secret id=apps_json,src="$BUILD_DIR/apps.json" \
  --build-arg FRAPPE_BRANCH="$FRAPPE_BRANCH" \
  --build-arg CACHE_BUST="$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid)" \
  .

# Never trust the build: prove the app is in the image before deploying it.
echo "=== apps in image (must list frappe, helpdesk, telephony) ==="
sudo docker run --rm --entrypoint ls "$IMAGE_TAG" -1 /home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps
sudo docker run --rm --entrypoint /home/frappe/frappe-bench/env/bin/python "$IMAGE_TAG" \
  -c "import helpdesk, telephony; print('IMPORT OK:', helpdesk.__file__)"
EOF
chmod +x build-image.sh
sed -i 's|^  image: ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0$|  # NOT ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk:v1.29.0 — that image does NOT contain the helpdesk\n  # app (bare frappe bench). Build it first with ./build-image.sh on the VM.\n  image: helpdesk-local:v1.29.0|' docker-compose.yml
sed -n '1,6p' docker-compose.yml

content.text: All four checks pass. Now recording what this deploy learned into `redu.md` — the platform notes are explicit that the merge never writes new quirks, so these have to be typed in by hand or they're lost:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='redu.md'
s=open(p).read()

anchor = '  - "⛔⛔ THE IMAGE TAG DOES NOT NAME THE SOURCE TREE'
assert anchor in s, "anchor missing"

new_quirks = '''  - "⛔⛔⛔ THE PUBLISHED ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk IMAGES DO NOT CONTAIN FRAPPE HELPDESK. THIS IS THE ONE THAT BREAKS THE DEPLOY, AND EVERY OTHER LINE IN THIS FILE ASSUMED THE OPPOSITE. Verified 2026-08-20 on v1.29.0, stable, main AND v1.28.1: /home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps contains ONLY \\"frappe\\", /home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets has no helpdesk directory, `find / -type d -name helpdesk` returns nothing, and the bench env python raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named helpdesk. They are a bare Frappe bench published under the helpdesk name. bench new-site therefore creates the database, installs frappe, and dies at --install-app helpdesk with `Could not find app \\"helpdesk\\"`. The earlier claim in this file that both apps are already inside the image was read from the BUILD WORKFLOW and never checked against the artefact. ⛔ DO NOT DEPLOY A PUBLISHED TAG. Build the image yourself with ./build-image.sh and prove `import helpdesk` works BEFORE composing anything."
  - "⛔⛔ THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH ALSO TELLS YOU HOW TO BUILD IT: helpdesk .github/workflows/build.yml passes the apps list as --build-arg APPS_JSON_BASE64, but frappe_docker images/layered/Containerfile now reads it from a BUILDKIT SECRET MOUNT: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=apps_json,target=/opt/frappe/apps.json` then `--apps_path=/opt/frappe/apps.json`. Docker does NOT error on a build-arg nothing consumes, so the build silently yields a frappe-only bench and pushes it under the release tag. Build with `--secret id=apps_json,src=apps.json` and a PLAIN JSON file (not base64). ⚠️ Upstream is still shipping broken images this way, so this is not a one-off bad tag and a newer tag will NOT fix it."
  - "⛔ CACHE_BUST IS LOAD-BEARING WHEN YOU REBUILD, AND ITS ABSENCE LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE THE BUG YOU ARE FIXING. A secret mount does NOT invalidate the BuildKit layer cache. After a first (frappe-only) build, adding --secret alone re-runs with every step CACHED and produces the SAME broken image in about two minutes, which reads as \\"the fix did not work\\". The Containerfile declares ARG CACHE_BUST for this; pass a fresh value. A real build takes roughly 10 minutes on m1.large; a suspiciously fast one means you got the cache."
  - "⛔ RE-RUNNING create-site AFTER A FAILURE NEEDS TWO THINGS CLEARED, NOT ONE. The compose guards on `if [ -d sites/$$SITE_NAME ]`, so the partial site directory makes a retry SKIP creation silently. Removing only that then fails with `Exception: Database _<hash> already exists` from frappe/database/mariadb/setup_db.py, because the database survives on the db-data volume and setup_database refuses to reuse it. Clear BOTH: rm -rf the site dir from the sites volume AND drop the database plus its user as root. Then `docker compose up -d`."
  - "THE MARIADB CLIENT IS CALLED mariadb, NOT mysql, IN mariadb:11.8.8. `docker compose exec db mysql -uroot ...` fails with `exec: \\"mysql\\": executable file not found in $PATH`, which reads like a broken container rather than a renamed binary. Use `mariadb -uroot -p\\"$DB_ROOT_PASSWORD\\"`."
  - "THE VERIFY SCRIPT'S CHECK 3 STRING IS VERSION-DEPENDENT AND WENT STALE. frappe 15.116+ refuses a bad password with HTTP 401 and `Invalid login credentials`; the script asserted the older `Incorrect password`, so a CORRECTLY refused default login reported INCONCLUSIVE. The script now accepts either string and still treats an unrecognised body as inconclusive, which is the right shape: a bare 401 does not prove the refusal happened for the right reason."
  - "⛔ IF create-site FAILS, THE redu DEPLOYMENT ROW GOES TERMINAL AND REPAIRING THE VM DOES NOT BRING IT BACK. Measured here: the probe never saw port 8080 (nothing was listening, because backend and frontend never start when create-site exits non-zero), so redu recorded status=error, phase=failed, terminal=true, and its build_log is frozen on the ORIGINAL failure. ## Your instance

**https://frappe-helpdesk-38ywi8ku.redu.cloud/helpdesk**

| | |
|---|---|
| Username | `Administrator` |

Both passwords are in `.env` (chmod 600). The bare hostname serves `<title>Login</title>` and `/helpdesk` serves the app — that's the documented behaviour, not a misconfiguration.

All four gated checks pass: [REDACTED:value] SPA serves, your generated password works, the README's `Administrator`/`admin` default is refused (401), and anonymous signup is refused (417).

## The recipe was wrong, and it was fatal

**`ghcr.io/frappe/helpdesk` does not contain Frappe Helpdesk.** I verified it on `v1.29.0`, `stable`, `main` and `v1.28.1` — every one is a bare Frappe bench: `apps/` holds only `frappe`, and `import helpdesk` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. So `bench new-site` created the database, installed frappe, then died at `--install-app helpdesk`.

The cause is upstream: helpdesk's build workflow passes the app list as `--build-arg APPS_JSON_BASE64`, but frappe_docker's `Containerfile` now reads it from a **BuildKit secret mount**. Docker doesn't error on a build-arg nothing consumes, so the build silently publishes a frappe-only image under the release tag. `redu.md` asserted "both are already inside the image" — that was read from the workflow, never checked against the artifact.

I built the image on the VM with `--secret id=apps_json` instead, pinning helpdesk to the **v1.29.0 tag** rather than the moving `main` branch upstream uses. The site now reports `helpdesk 1.29.0`, `telephony 0.0.1`, `frappe 15.118.0`. (`CACHE_BUST` matters — a secret mount doesn't invalidate the layer cache, so my first "fixed" rebuild came back fully cached and reproduced the same broken image.)

## One thing you should know

**redu's deployment row for `492` says `status: error, terminal: true`.** The first `create-site` failure meant nothing listened on 8080, so the probe window closed and the record went terminal. I repaired the stack over SSH afterwards and it's verified working, but redu won't reopen a terminal record — `containers_summary` shows the live truth, `status` doesn't. Treat it as a working instance with a stale platform row.

## Measured (`redu.md` said these were unmeasured)

1742 MB RAM used of 7941 MB idle — m1.large is generous on RAM; disk is what justifies it. 23 GB of 77 GB used, including the build cache. Zero OOM kills.

## Two things left, both yours

- **No off-VM backup.** Your ticket data lives on this VM's volumes and does not survive `delete_deployment`, with no managed database to recover from. This matters more here than on any other entry in that library.
- **No support mailbox** — tickets arrive by IMAP polling; add an Email Account in the UI.

I updated `redu.md` with 8 new quirks (the image defect, the secret-mount build, the cache trap, the two-part failure cleanup, the `mariadb` vs `mysql` rename, the stale verify string, the terminal-row behaviour, and the measurements), fixed `verify.sh`'s outdated `Incorrect password` assertion, and replaced the estimate in `redu-deploy-plan.md` with the as-deployed record. Note `build-image.sh` must be run on the VM before `docker compose up` — a redeploy to a fresh VM will fail without it, since the working image exists only locally.
